newsitem.title: USA: High-grade US corporate bond deals crowd calendar.
newsitem.headline: High-grade US corporate bond deals crowd calendar.

text.p: Corporate issuers are quickly filling up this week's calendar with new investment-grade bond offerings, lured by a recent rally in U.S. interest rates, syndicate sources said.

High-profile companies such as Philip Morris Cos Inc, SBC Communications Inc unit Southwestern Bell Telephone, and Federated Department Stores Inc are all expected to launch sizable debt deals on Tuesday.
In the junk bond market, new issue action is likely to be slow today, as most offerings are slated for later in the week.

Returning to the primary market for investment-grade debt, two competitive bid offerings are expected as early as today. They include a $350 million offering of 10-year debt from PNC Bank Corp, and a $500 million offering of five-year debt from Associates First Capital Corp.
Additionally, Johnson Controls Inc is expected to sell $150 million in 20-year bullet debt, rated A2/A, via JP Morgan Securities.
Texas Gas Transmission Corp, a unit of Williams Cos, is also rumored to be readying a $100 million 30-year bullet offering.

Private Export Funding Corp is expected to sell $100 million in 10-year AAA/AAA debt via Citicorp Securities Inc on Wednesday. Price talk on the deal is 24-25 basis points over comparable Treasuries, market sources said.
Dealers said issuers were tempted to sell long-duration bonds in order to capitalize on bullish investor sentiment about the direction of interest rates.

"Given the recent highs we've seen in the Treasury market, we wouldn't be surprised is someone else jumps in with a century bond," a syndicate source said, referring to yesterday's 100-year bond issue from Federal Express Corp.
The high-yield bond market has been focusing on price talk for this week's mega-offering from Iridium LLC, a company building a global satellite communications network.
Price talk on the $500 million seven-year senior note tranche is 12-12.5 percent over Treasuries.
Iridium's $250 million zero coupon tranche is expected to be priced 1.25-1.50 percent over the cash-pay tranche.
The deal will also include warrants to purchase 1.25-1.50 percent of the equity in Iridium World, the publicly traded subsidiary of Iridium LLC. The warrants will be split between the two tranches.
The market was rife with conflicting rumors about how the high-profile offering is being received by investors.

"Market reaction is neutral, partly because this is a very complicated deal. No one is saying it's terrific, but it's probably good enough to get done," said one high-yield bond telecommunications analyst.
